segments.he: רבינו ז"ל אמר שהוא אוהב שענינו יבא על לבות של ליטוואקיס כי יש להם לב חזק והם עקשנים גדולים וזה מעלה גדולה בעבודת השם "זיין זאך שאל איבער גיין אוף ליטוושי הערצער".
segments.en:
At the home of the grandson of Reb Pinchas of Koritz — they had printed volumes of the Zohar and other works that were among the ten books forbidden to be printed in Russia. They were seized and imprisoned in Petersburg, and sentenced as rebels against the government. They sat in heavy imprisonment for twenty-one years. Once they were led out to be beaten in the gauntlet — led between rows of many soldiers who beat them with rods from both sides as they walked. One dropped his hat and stopped to pick it up — and received many extra blows. Together with them was a priest who had sinned and was imprisoned. This priest would send complaints to the king each time — and each time he sent such a complaint, they placed him in heavier imprisonment and beat him. Seeing this, the Jewish prisoners made no complaint throughout all those years.

Only at the end did a senior government official happen to encounter them, found favor in their eyes, and gave them counsel: it was known to him that the king was by nature compassionate — possessed of a mercy so great that even someone utterly guilty could, by appealing to this mercy, be forgiven entirely. Therefore they should write a petition to the emperor — not mentioning that they were innocent or had done no wrong, and not writing complaints. On the contrary: they should write that in truth they admit they had sinned — but not with intent to defy the king's authority. And they had already received punishment — sitting so many years in prison and being beaten — and they were old and weak. And knowing that the king possesses such mercy that even one entirely guilty by strict law can be forgiven — therefore they beseech his mercy. And so they did. And immediately a decree came to release them entirely.

Reb Nachman of Tulchin spoke of this and said: malkus d'ara k'ein malkus d'rakiya [earthly kingship parallels heavenly kingship] — and he aroused our fellowship to know from this how to plead before Hashem: not to complain about the measure of strict judgment and say "I did not sin" — but on the contrary, to say: "Truly I have sinned and transgressed and did such-and-such — but not with intent to anger You — and the evil inclination within prevented me — and I have already received and accepted my suffering — and I am weak and cannot endure more. But I know that You possess a mercy such that even one who has sinned greatly and has no legal merit whatsoever — You can show mercy and forgive entirely. Therefore I beseech You that You awaken this mercy upon me and forgive me."
